title: Autonomic SafePath Throttler and Fallback Scripting
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Goal: Design and implement an autonomous "SafePath" throttler that sits upstream of per-dependency/per-model/per-tenant circuit logic to provide a predictable, SLO-aligned soft-trip surface and scripted safe fallbacks. The feature should reduce customer-visible errors during overload/failure windows by combining: 1) short-window quantile trip thresholds tied to SLO objectives, 2) hysteresis and decay profiles to avoid flapping, 3) deterministic load-shedding policies with per-tenant fairness, and 4) scripted fallback chains (model variants, regional reroutes, cached responses) with documented quality trade-offs.

Background: Recent incidents showed two recurring failure modes: (A) noisy upstream spikes that caused broad model-level circuit trips that were slow to recover, and (B) tenant-specific hot-paths that exhausted capacity and forced blunt global throttles. Existing protective mechanisms (single global circuit per-model and coarse tenant rate limits) lack SLO-awareness and do not expose clear runbooks for safe fallbacks. This ticket aims to introduce a composable throttler layer that harmonizes thresholds across dependency, model, and tenant dimensions and drives fallback routing scripts in Console and the routing decision engine.

Key requirements:
- SLO-aligned trip calculus: support percent-error and p95/p99 latency thresholds expressed relative to per-route SLOs and configurable guardrails (e.g., 2x breach over 30s triggers soft-trip).
- Multi-dimensional trips: allow trip evaluation by dependency, model variant, and tenant (configurable aggregation keys).
- Hysteresis and decay: implement configurable cool-downs and exponential decay windows to prevent oscillations; provide transparent state transitions in telemetry.
- Fair load shedding: proportional shedding across tenants using token-bucket equivalents and weighted cohort fairness to avoid starving small customers.
- Scripted fallback chains: define ordered fallbacks (e.g., model-quantized-variant -> regional fallback -> cached prefix -> limited stub response) with explicit quality-cost metadata and max-fallback-depth.
- Observability: per-trip event logs, sampling of pre- and post-fallback responses, dashboards for trip correlation with infra metrics and request traces, and automated alerts tied to SLO regressions.
- Safety: ability to dry-run in shadow mode, gradual rollout flags, kill-switch in Console, and an auto-revert backoff when downstream success rates improve.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: implementation of on-prem control plane changes (will be a follow-up), UI polish for Console beyond essential rollout controls, and billing changes for switched routes.

Deliverables:
- Design doc (Confluence link) with threshold heuristics and simulation results.
- Runtime library implementing SafePath throttler and fallback script interpreter (Go + Rust components).
- Metrics and tracing schema, Grafana dashboards, and a runbook for incident response.
- Canary rollout plan, including shadow mode and progressive traffic shifts.

Success criteria:
- During controlled load tests, reduce P99 error amplification after upstream spike by >= 60% compared to baseline (no SafePath).
- No increase in mean latency beyond 10% for non-shed requests under degraded conditions.
- Console rollout with shadow mode enabled and safe unroll on first failure.

Notes on API and config: SafePath rules will be represented as JSON scripts stored in the config store. Each rule includes selectors (model/dependency/tenant), trip expression (window, metric, threshold), hysteresis params, shedding policy (percentage or token budget), and fallback chain array with annotated quality labels. The routing engine will evaluate selectors and apply the highest-priority matching rule.
